answer: Each new agent must post collateral scaled to its privileges, locked against a named third-party attestor slashed if it cheats. One wallet can spin up a thousand puppets, but each needs its own backer with money at risk, so the attacker pays that fee a thousand times, not once. A rent-a-crowd attestor is easy to spot: its vouching graph folds into one cluster once scoring walks the links. The beacon of real reputation is costly to fake; a rented fleet is a dune that erodes when one member defaults. The jetty admits only boats carrying real weight, so forging identity stops paying.
